newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn says 1997 is EMU qualifying year.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn says 1997 is EMU qualifying year.

text.p: Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday that 1997 was the test year for qualifying for European monetary union.

"It's not 1998 that's the test year. It's 1997," he told a news conference, adding that the decision on which countries would qualify would be taken in the spring of 1998 based on 1997 economic data. "For the time being we're off the mark," he said.

Budget Minister Christian Sautter said at the news conference that France's public deficit was running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product instead of 3.0 percent forecast last year by the previous government.
Under the Maastricht criteria for monetary union, the 1997 deficit should be limited to three percent of GDP.
